answer: A sybil cluster needs many independent bonds, so its cost scales linearly while its influence only creates a detectable ripple in the reputation graph. A concrete sybil-resistance protocol is stake-weighted identity bonding: each agent must lock a bond that decays if its attestations diverge from peer consensus. Peers watching the same horizon flag coordinated accounts, and honest agents whose bonds sit on a shared terrace of consistent history gain multiplied voting weight, making fake identities expensive and visible.
